source.title: Sparse Reward Subsystem in Large Language Models
source.authors: Guowei Xu; Mert Yuksekgonul; James Y. Zou

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies sparse reward-related signals in neurons, but does not test whether neuron poles have one or two human-nameable jobs, test explanations on held-out activations, or evaluate the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern neurons selected to predict value or TD error. They do not measure single-job interpretability, explanation accuracy on new activations, the InceptionV1 examples, or attribution-graph reconstruction. The reward-probe pruning and intervention findings are recorded as related findings outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study finds sparse neuron subsets (via probe L1 pruning) that predict value and TD error, and ablates them. It does not audit what share of neuron poles have one nameable job. It does not score neuron explanations on held-out activations, examine InceptionV1, or build neuron attribution graphs. Its single-neuron visualization (layer 5 neuron 1517) is illustrative, not a share. It invokes superposition only as motivation for sparsity.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that reward information is concentrated in sparse value and dopamine neurons, which are causally specific and transfer across datasets and models. They show uses for confidence prediction and as a process reward model. They do not address per-neuron interpretability shares.
record.recipe_differences: Uses reward probes, input-dimension pruning, and neuron ablations; it does not perform the neuron-pole explanation and held-out activation testing in the claim's original audit.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curves and results vary across model, layer, dataset, and pruning ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Under 1% of hidden dimensions suffice for a probe to predict terminal reward (AUC stable under pruning) in several models. Zeroing the top 1% value neurons in Qwen-2.5-7B-SimpleRL-Zoo drops MATH500 accuracy from 75.2% to 20.3% on average, versus 74.6% for random neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reward-related information in LLM hidden states is concentrated in a sparse, causally important subset of neurons.

record.problems: The paper notes that it has not investigated similar phenomena in models larger than 32B. The pruning-curve values are presented in plots without numeric values in the text; intervention results have no uncertainty estimates stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other pruning curves, dataset/model robustness plots, transferability IoU curves, dopamine-neuron pruning results, and additional intervention/control rows were omitted because they concern reward-prediction signals rather than the claim versions' interpretability measures.

untested.parts: All: share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one, two or unknown jobs.
All: interpretable-neuron shares across models and scales (paper notes no models above 32B).
All: InceptionV1 polysemantic examples and recursive generalization.
All: architecture, regularization or tool effects on interpretability share.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models.
All: whether activating-example explanations predict activations elsewhere.

record.verdict_notes: Random and NTP-neuron control columns in Table 2 are not rows; they could be added as controls, but this is not needed for this claim. The 'neurons' here are hidden-state (residual) dimensions selected by probe weights, not MLP neuron poles as in V1.

versions.untested_parts: The share of poles with one or two jobs and the share not understood.
Interpretable-pole shares across models, architectures, or scales, including models up to trillions of parameters.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain interpretability rates, including the InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Whether attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons explain behaviour without a replacement model or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples fail to predict activation on other examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-14B-SimpleRL-Zoo
rows.operation_detail: Pruned value-probe input dimensions in order of lowest L1 weight norm and evaluated AUC for predicting terminal reward from the initial-position hidden state.
rows.measure: AUC of the pruned value probe predicting terminal reward
rows.value: figure only; text says the AUC curves did not show a significant decline as pruning proceeded, and that less than 1% of neurons sufficed
rows.uncertainty: Shaded uncertainty regions; numeric uncertainty not stated
rows.note: This is sparse encoding of a reward-prediction signal, not a measure of whether a neuron has one nameable job.
rows.check: The probe is pruned over input dimensions of the residual hidden state, not neuron poles. AUC stability says nothing about single-job interpretability. Baseline AUC is not stated, and the value is figure-only.
